spans.s:
r. 1st cl. (यजति)
1 To worship a deity.
2 To associate with.
3 To present or endow.

m. (-जः)
Boiled rice, or generally, food.
E.
यज to present, aff. घञ्

mfn. (-जन्-जन्ती-जत्)
Sacrificing, worshipping.
E.
यज to worship, शतृ aff.

m. (-तः)
The officiating priest at a sacrifice.
E.
यज to worship, अतच् aff.

m. (-त्रः)
A Brahman who has maintained his consecrated fire.
E.
यज to sacrifice, अत्रन् Uṇādi aff.

n. (-नं)
Offering sacrifices, performing worship.
E.
यज to worship, ल्युट् aff.

n. (-नं)
Conducting a sacrifice or causing its performance.
E.
यज to worship, causal form, aff. ल्युट्.

m. (-न्तः)
A sacrificer, a worshipper.
E.
यज to sacrifice, aff. झच्.

mfn. (-नः-ना-नं)
Worshipping.
m. (-नः)
An employer of priests at a sacrifice, the person who institutes its performance, and pays the expence of it.
E.
यज to worship, शानच् aff. of the present participle, with मक् augment.

m. (-कः)
A donor, a benefactor, a liberal giver of presents, &c.
E.
यज to present, Uṇādi aff. आकन्.

m. (-कः)
1 An officiating priest, a Brahman who conducts any part of a sacrifice.
2 A royal elephant.
3 A furious elephant.
E.
यज to worship, ण्वुल् aff.

m. (-जिः)
A sacrificer, one who institutes or performs a sacrifice.
E.
यज to sacrifice, aff. इन्.

m. (-जिः)
A sacrificer, an institutor of sacrificial ceremonies.
E.
यज to sacrifice, Uṇādi aff. इञ्.

n. (-दं)
The Yajur Veda: see the next.
E.
ययुस्, and वेद a Veda.

n. (-जुः)
The Yajur or Yajuṣ, one of the four Vedas; it is divided into two principal portions, the white and black, or Vājasaneyi and Taittirīya, the former of which is attributed to the saint YĀJÑAVALKYA, to whom it was revealed by the sun, in the form of a horse; and the latter to TITTIRI, to whom it was communicated by YĀSKA, the first pupil of its original author, the sage VAIŚAMPĀYANA: according to the Purāṇas, the Taittirīya portion was named from Tittiri a partridge; the disciples of VAIŚAMPĀYANA being changed into those birds, to pick up the texts of the Veda, as they were disgorged in a tangible shape by YĀJÑAVALKYA, at the command of VAIŚAMPĀYANA: both portions of this Veda are very full on the subject of religious rites, and the prayers peculiar to it, are chiefly in measured and poetical prose.
E.
यज to worship, Uṇādi aff. उसि.

m. (-ज्ञः)
A sacrifice, a ceremony in which oblations are presented.
E.
यज to worship, aff. नङ्.

n. (-र्म्म)
Any sacrificial act or ceremony.
E.
यज्ञ, and कर्म्मन् act.

m. (-कृत्)
A sacrificer, a worshipper, or priest conducting a sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and कृत् who makes.

m. (-ध्रुक्)
A Rākṣasa, an imp.
E.
यज्ञ, and द्रुह् to wrong, क्विप् aff.

m. (-शुः)
1 A horse.
2 Any animal offered in sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ a sacrifice, and पशु an animal.

n. (-त्रं)
A sacrificial vessel.
E.
यज्ञ, and पात्र a vessel.

m. (-षः)
A name of VIṢṆU.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and पुरुष man or male.

n. (-नं)
A sacrificial vessel.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and भाजन vessel.

f. (-मिः)
Place prepared for a sacrifice, or where it is offered.
E.
यज्ञ, and भूमि land.

m. (-हः)
VIṢṆU in the boar incarnation.
E.
यज्ञ, and वराह the boar.

m. (-टः)
A place prepared and enclosed for a sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ a sacrifice, and वाट inclosure.

mfn. (-ष्टः-ष्टा-ष्टं)
What is left from a sacrifice or oblation.
E.
यज्ञ, and शिष्ट remainder.

n. (-षः)
The reliques of a sacrifice or oblation.
E.
यज्ञ, and शेष remainder.

m. (-रः)
The glomerous fig tree, (Ficus glomerata, Rox.)
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and सार essence.

f. (-द्धिः)
1 Performance of sacrifice.
2 Obtaining the objects of a sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ, and सिद्धि accomplishment.

n. (-त्रं)
The characteristic thread, worn by the three principal classes of Hindus.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and सूत्र thread.

n. (-नं)
A place of sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ, and स्थान place.

m. (-ङ्गः)
1 The glomerous fig, (Ficus glomerata, Rox.)
2 A plant, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
3 A part of any sacrificial ceremony.
E.
यज्ञ a sacrifice, and अङ्ग a member.

m. (-न्तः)
A supplementary sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञ the principal, and अन्त end, finish.

m. (-रिः)
1 A name of Ś

IVA.
2

A demon, a goblin.
E.
यज्ञ a sacrifice, and अरि enemy.

m. (-कः)
The Pālaś tree, (Butea frondosa.)
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, ठक् aff.

m. (-कः)
1 A sacrificer, an institutor of a sacrifice.
2 An officiating priest at a sacrificial ceremony.
3 Kuśa or sacrificial grass.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and ठक् aff.

mfn. (-यः-या-यं)
Proper for or suitable to a sacrifice.
m. (-यः)
The third Yug or age.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and घ aff.

mfn. (-यः-यी-यं)
Fit for sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञिय, and अण added.

f. (-शः)
The country of the Hindus; those districts in which the ritual and institutes of the Hindu system are enforced; properly the country in which the black deer or antelope is native.
E.
यज्ञिय sacrificial, and देश a country.

f. (-ला)
A temple, a shrine, a place of sacrifice.
E.
यज्ञिय to be sacrificed, (where,) and शाला hall.

m. (-रः)
The glomerous fig tree, (Ficus glomerata, Rox.)
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and उडुम्बर the same.

n. (-तं)
The sacrificial cord, originally worn by the three principal casts of Hindus: at present from the loss of the pure Kṣatriya and Vaiśya casts in Bengal, confined to the Brahmanical order.
E.
यज्ञ sacrifice, and उपवीत thread.

m. (-ती)
A Brahman, &c. invested with the sacred thread.
E.
यज्ञोपवीत, and इनि aff.

m. (-ज्युः)
A Brahman, Conversant with the Yajur Veda.
E.
यज to worship, Uṇādi aff. युच्.

m. (-ज्वा)
A sacrificer in due form, or agreeably to the ritual of the Vedas.
E.
यज to worship, वनिप् aff.

m. (-तिः)
The moon.
E.
यज्वन् a sacrificer in the sixth case plural, and पति master.

m. (-जी)
Sacrificing, one who officiates at a sacrifice.
E.
यज to sacrifice, घिनुण् aff.

mfn. (-ज्यः-ज्या-ज्यं)
To be offered or sacrificed.
m. (-ज्यः)
A sacrificer, the person for whom it is performed.
n. (-ज्यं)
Property or presents derived from officiating at sacrifices.
E.
यज to worship, ण्य aff.

mfn. (-षः-षी-षं)
Belonging to or relating to the Yajur Veda.
E.
यजुर or यजुस् the Veda, and अण् aff.

m. (-त्तिः)
KUVERA.
E.
यज्ञदत्त a proper name, and इञ् aff. of descent.

m. (-ल्क्यः)
A celebrated saint and legislator; the supposed author of a celebrated code of laws, and the first reputed teacher of the white portion of the Yajur Veda revealed to him by the sun.
E.
यज्ञवल्क the father of the saint, and ष्यञ् aff.

f. (-नी)
A name of DRAUPADĪ, the wife of the Pāṇḍus.
E.
यज्ञसेन the father of the princess, and अण् patronymic aff., ङीष् fem. aff.

n. (-क्यं)
Sacrifice, sacrificial ceremonies.
E.
याज्ञिक a sacrificer, and यञ् aff.
